body_markdown:
I will be frank about the hardest part of building an AI labeling workforce. Sourcing talent is easy, but manually paying those contractors across multiple time zones quickly becomes a nightmare. People always ask what is data annotation, yet they ignore the administrative friction of global tax compliance and currency conversion.


My position: treat payouts as core infrastructure from day one. Every contributor you onboard without identity checks, tax forms, and a local payout method becomes a manual ticket for your finance team. This guide is for teams building annotation programs, not people looking for annotation work.


**TLDR:**


- AI data annotation requires rich metadata, while basic data labeling assigns a single tag.
- Manual payouts break down fast when your workforce spans multiple time zones.
- You must clear KYC checks before the first task begins to stop fraud.
- The Dots API executes identity verification and payouts across 190+ countries.


## What Is Data Annotation?


This guide is built for ops teams, not side-income seekers. If you want a basic what is a data annotation job explainer for side income, stop reading. Operations teams building global workforces must understand how these payout mechanics scale.


Data annotation is the process of labeling information so an AI model can process it. It acts as a short glossary entry for machines. Reviewers tag images of street signs or categorize text sentiment.


## AI Data Annotation vs. Data Labeling


You often hear data labeling and AI data annotation used interchangeably. For ops leaders structuring workflows, distinguishing these terms prevents budget drain.


Data labeling assigns a single tag to a raw asset. Think of a binary categorization task: a reviewer flags a submitted audio file as clear or distorted.


When you ask what is data annotation in AI, the scope expands. This process requires adding rich metadata and contextual layers.


## The Main Types of Data Annotation


The market for data annotation tools will grow from[USD 2.1 billion](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/data-annotation-tools-market) in 2026 to USD 10.3 billion by 2033. AI models process varied inputs, requiring specific types of data annotation to function.


If you need a what is data annotation breakdown by format, the work spans five main categories. Image tasks involve drawing bounding boxes around medical scans, while text labeling identifies entities in contracts. Audio and video tasks involve transcribing spoken calls or tracking pedestrian movement across frames. Finally, human feedback or ranking tasks support Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) by scoring AI-generated responses.

## Who Does the Data Annotation Work?


When building an AI product, you must decide how to staff your labeling projects. The[global data labeling market](https://straitsresearch.com/report/data-collection-and-labeling-market) is projected to grow rapidly over the next decade. Within this growing sector, companies rely on three primary groups to handle the work:


- In-house teams
- Managed vendors
- Distributed contributor workforces


## What Running a Contributor Workforce Involves


Sourcing talent for data annotation jobs is only the first step. You must also build an infrastructure to verify, track, and compensate thousands of international contributors. Running a data annotation company requires full workforce management:


- Identity verification: You have to onboard each worker securely through[KYC (Know Your Customer) checks](https://usedots.com/blog/what-is-kyc-banking-payouts/) before the first task begins to prevent fraud.
- Global tax compliance: You must collect the right[foreign contractor withholding tax](https://usedots.com/blog/guide-to-us-tax-withholding-for-foreign-contractors/) forms.
- Payout routing: You must run contractor payouts across countries on the local rails they can actually use.


## How to Pay International Contractors for Annotation Work


When your workforce spans multiple time zones, manual payouts break down fast. Sourcing talent is the easy part. Moving those funds across borders introduces severe administrative friction.


What are payment rails? They are the networks that move money between accounts, such as ACH (US batch bank transfers), RTP (Real-Time Payments), SWIFT (international bank messaging), and local e-wallets. You cannot rely on a single domestic bank rail when contributors live across dozens of jurisdictions, and foreign business entities may need a[W-8BEN-E form](https://usedots.com/blog/w-8ben-e-form-guide/) (foreign status certification form) on file before you can pay them.


Before accepting tasks, workers ask how you route their earnings, and individual contributors abroad will often need to complete a[W-8BEN form](https://usedots.com/blog/what-is-a-w-8ben-form/) (foreign status certification form) first. A competitive data annotator salary per month loses its value if hidden conversion fees consume the payout, which is why so many ops teams look for better ways to[pay international contractors](https://usedots.com/blog/how-to-pay-international-contractors-2/) .

## FAQ


### Dots vs. separate payment gateways for a data annotation company?


Dots natively handles both global disbursements and compliance, replacing fragmented tech stacks. Stitching together separate payment gateways and identity tools introduces severe administrative friction when scaling an international workforce.


A typical fragmented stack pairs a KYC (Know Your Customer) vendor for identity checks, a separate processor for ACH (US batch bank transfers) or SWIFT (international bank messaging) transfers, a tax tool for W-8BEN and W-9 collection, and a spreadsheet to track who got paid. Each piece needs its own contract, support queue, and reconciliation step, and a mismatch between systems can delay a contributor's payout by days.


With Dots, identity verification, tax form collection, and payout routing run through one connection, so a reviewer in Manila and a transcriber in Lagos both clear onboarding and receive funds through the same workflow. Finance teams skip the manual cross-checking between vendors, and support tickets about missing payments drop because the contributor portal shows status in one place instead of three.


### Can I build a data annotation job payout flow with Dots without a separate KYC provider?


Yes. The Dots API verifies worker identity across more than 190 countries through a single connection. You clear contributors through KYC checks before they accept their first task, eliminating the need to integrate and manage a secondary vendor.


A typical flow looks like this: a contributor signs up, submits a government ID and a selfie match, and the Dots API returns a verification result in seconds rather than days. Once cleared, that same profile carries forward to collect the correct tax form, whether a W-9 (US tax identification form) for domestic contractors or a W-8BEN (foreign status certification form) for contributors abroad. The contributor then picks a payout method from the portal, such as a bank transfer, PayPal, or a local e-wallet, based on what their country supports. For an annotation program onboarding hundreds of reviewers weekly, this removes manual document review, spreadsheet tracking, and the back-and-forth of chasing missing tax paperwork before the first paid task.


### How do I pay international contractors without eroding their data annotator salary per month?


Route their earnings through local payment networks instead of relying on a single domestic bank rail. Dots provides a customized portal where contributors choose their preferred payout method, preventing hidden cross-border conversion fees from consuming their pay.


In practice, a contributor in the Philippines might choose a local e-wallet such as GCash, while a contractor in Kenya opts for mobile money and a contractor in Germany prefers a SEPA bank transfer. Picking the rail that matches local banking habits cuts the fees and delays that a single SWIFT transfer would add. Before the first payout, collect a W-8BEN form (foreign status certification form) from each non-US contributor so withholding is calculated correctly from the start. Pair that with KYC (Know Your Customer) checks at onboarding, and you avoid the fraud and compliance gaps that force manual intervention later. Batching payouts weekly or biweekly rather than per task also reduces the number of transfers, which keeps per-transaction fees from eating into smaller annotation payments.
